original_question: What is the deeper conceptual reason that Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials can violate locality, or equivalently the Weyl-type locality behavior that underlies the usual hbar^{-d} semiclassical scale?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, unnumbered open-ended sentence immediately after Question 2: "An even vaguer question is to understand from a more conceptual point of view the deeper reason behind a potential violation of locality." This is the closest paper-faithful target of your draft. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual intent: it asks for a conceptual explanation rather than a new estimate, and it correctly ties locality failure to the semiclassical ħ^{-d} scale. That is exactly the theme of §2 and, almost verbatim, of the unnumbered sentence after Question 2 in §2.1. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's setting is the semiclassical Schrödinger operator H_{ħ,V}=-ħ^2Δ+V on L^2(ℝ^d), with ħ∈(0,1], V:ℝ^d→ℂ locally regular enough to define an m-sectorial operator, and V decaying at infinity so that the spectrum in ℂ\[0,∞) consists of isolated eigenvalues E_j of finite algebraic multiplicity. Your draft does not state this ambient analytic setting. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The paper's notion of "locality" is not physical/QFT locality; it means that eigenvalue sums are controlled by a linear integral of the potential, so disjoint pieces of V contribute additively. The paper says this is closely related to the appearance of ħ^{-d}. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The nearby quantitative object is the eigenvalue sum ∑_j |E_j|^{-σ}δ(E_j)^{γ+σ}, where δ(E):=dist(E,[0,∞)). Your draft does not name this sum or define δ. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The paper's immediately surrounding regime is 0≤σ≤d/2 and γ>0 in Question 2, because that is where the authors ask whether higher-dimensional examples with growth ≫ħ^{-d} exist. Your draft omits these quantifiers. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The asymptotic quantifier is as ħ→0; in the cited one-dimensional examples, the lower bounds hold for all sufficiently small ħ>0. Your draft mentions the scale but not the precise asymptotic regime. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

The nearby discussion emphasizes a possible threshold at σ=d/2 for the validity versus failure of an O(ħ^{-d}) bound; this threshold is part of the paper's intended scope around the conceptual question. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

Section 2.2 gives a concrete formal manifestation of loss of locality: all known nonlocal bounds of the form (9) have exponent α/γ>1, so the right side is a power strictly greater than 1 of the integral of |V|^{γ+d/2}, and the power of ħ^{-1} exceeds d. Your draft points in this direction, but the paper does not state this as a literal equivalence theorem; it is supporting context. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))

There are no polynomial homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency assumptions anywhere in this paper. The hidden data that matter here are instead d, γ, σ, the integrability class V∈L^{γ+d/2}(ℝ^d) when comparing with Lieb–Thirring-type bounds, and the discrete-spectrum assumptions above. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
refined_question: For the semiclassical Schrödinger operator H_{ħ,V}=-ħ^2Δ+V in L^2(ℝ^d), where V:ℝ^d→ℂ is locally regular enough to make H_{ħ,V} m-sectorial and decays at infinity so that the eigenvalues E_j in ℂ\[0,∞) are discrete and counted with algebraic multiplicity, and with δ(E):=dist(E,[0,∞)), what structural mechanism explains the possible failure of locality in the paper's sense—namely, the failure of additive integral control at the Weyl/Lieb–Thirring semiclassical scale ħ^{-d} for sums of the form ∑_j |E_j|^{-σ}δ(E_j)^{γ+σ}—especially in the regime 0≤σ≤d/2 highlighted by the one-dimensional examples (6)–(8) and by the higher-dimensional existence problem in Question 2? ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
justification: This paper is organized around Questions 1–3, not around a Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3. Your draft does not primarily target Question 1 or Question 3; instead it almost paraphrases the final sentence of §2.1. The surrounding text is exactly the context needed to make that sentence stand alone: §2 defines locality as additive integral control and says it is closely related to the factor ħ^{-d}; §2.1 specifies the relevant sums, records the one-dimensional violations (6)–(8), and raises the σ=d/2 threshold issue; and §2.2 explains that known replacement bounds lose locality because the right side is a power >1 of the integral, which also forces a stronger power of ħ^{-1}. So the refined question stays with the paper's own conceptual target, but makes explicit the operator, notation, quantifiers, and scope that the original unnumbered sentence leaves implicit. ([nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz](https://nsa.fjfi.cvut.cz/problems/06_CIRM_2024/2024-02/2024-02_CIRM_Cuenin_Frank.pdf))
